name: godot
description:
Everything Gofer can do inside the open Godot editor. Every operation is named `domain.op` and goes in the `ops` list as its `op`, with its parameters beside it.
# session
Operations:
- session.status: Reports the session state, ports, engine version, and worktree. (not twice in one call: It takes no parameters, so a second one in the same call is the first one again.)
- session.start: Starts the editor session for the active task worktree. (not twice in one call: There is one editor session, so a second one in the same call is the first one again.)
- session.stop: Stops the editor session and removes the staged Gofer addon. (not twice in one call: There is one editor session, so a second one in the same call is the first one again.)
- session.get_state: Asks the addon for readiness, the open scene, its revision, and the dialog the editor is waiting on. (not twice in one call: It takes no parameters, so a second one in the same call is the first one again.)
- session.answer_dialog: Presses a button on the dialog the editor is waiting on, by its label — one of the `buttons` the dialog was reported with. (not twice in one call: One dialog is up at a time, and pressing a button clears it, so a second press has nothing to press.)
- session.undo: Undoes the last editor operation. (not twice in one call: One undo stack, walked in order: what the second call undoes depends on what the first one did.)
- session.redo: Redoes the last undone editor operation. (not twice in one call: One undo stack, walked in order: what the second call undoes depends on what the first one did.)

# scene
Operations:
- scene.list: Lists the scene files in the project. (not twice in one call: It takes no parameters, so a second one in the same call is the first one again.)
- scene.open: Opens a scene. (not twice in one call: One scene is open at a time, so a second one would act on whatever the first left open.)
- scene.create: Creates a scene and opens it.
- scene.get_tree: Returns the edited scene hierarchy and its revision.
- scene.save: Saves the edited scene. (not twice in one call: One scene is open at a time, so a second one would act on whatever the first left open.)
- scene.save_as: Saves the edited scene to a new path. (not twice in one call: One scene is open at a time, so a second one would act on whatever the first left open.)
- scene.reload: Reloads the edited scene from disk, discarding in-memory edits. (not twice in one call: One scene is open at a time, so a second one would act on whatever the first left open.)

# node
Operations:
- node.inspect: Inspects a node.
- node.create_nodes: Creates nodes, as one revision and one undo step.
- node.instantiate: Places an instance of a saved scene under a node.
- node.duplicate: Duplicates a node.
- node.rename: Renames a node.
- node.reparent: Reparents a node.
- node.change_type: Turns a node into one of another class, keeping its name, its place, its children, its groups, its script, and every stored property the new class also has.
- node.delete: Deletes a node.
- node.set_properties: Sets properties, as one revision and one undo step.
- node.add_to_group: Puts a node in a group the saved scene keeps.
- node.remove_from_group: Takes a node out of a group.
- node.connect_signal: Connects a node's signal to a method, as an editor connection the scene keeps.
- node.disconnect_signal: Removes a connection.
- node.set_cells: Paints tiles onto a TileMapLayer.
- node.get_cells: Reads back what a TileMapLayer holds.

# project
Operations:
- project.get_settings: Returns the project settings overview. (not twice in one call: It takes no parameters, so a second one in the same call is the first one again.)
- project.search_settings: Searches project settings by name.
- project.get_setting: Reads one project setting.
- project.set_setting: Writes one project setting.
- project.reset_setting: Resets a project setting to its default, and answers what that did: `changed`, the `previous` value and the `value` it reads as now.
- project.list_autoloads: Lists the configured autoloads. (not twice in one call: It takes no parameters, so a second one in the same call is the first one again.)
- project.set_autoload: Adds or updates an autoload.
- project.remove_autoload: Removes an autoload.
- project.list_input_actions: Lists the Input Map actions this project chose — its own, and the built-ins it overrode — with their events.
- project.set_input_action: Writes an input action.
- project.remove_input_action: Removes a project input action.
- project.reset_input_action: Drops the override of a built-in action.
- project.list_plugins: Lists the project's editor plugins. (not twice in one call: It takes no parameters, so a second one in the same call is the first one again.)
- project.set_plugin_enabled: Enables or disables a plugin.
- project.search_editor_settings: Searches machine-wide editor settings by name.
- project.get_editor_setting: Reads one machine-wide editor setting.
- project.set_editor_setting: Writes one machine-wide editor setting.

# resource
Operations:
- resource.list: Lists the files in the task worktree with their sizes.
- resource.rescan: Tells the editor filesystem about files that changed.
- resource.create_tileset: Cuts a texture into a TileSet and saves it.
- resource.create_texture: Draws a PNG and imports it, which is how a project with no art gets some.
- resource.create_shape: Saves a 2D collision shape as a resource.
- resource.describe_tileset: Reports what a saved TileSet holds.
- resource.move: Moves a file or directory inside the worktree.
- resource.delete: Deletes a file or directory, and Godot's own record of it — its `.uid`, an asset's `.import` — with it.

# script
Operations:
- script.list: Lists the GDScript files in the worktree with their size.
- script.open: Opens a script as a language-server document.
- script.update: Reports an in-memory buffer change.
- script.edit: Changes existing scripts by replacing exact text, and answers with each file's diagnostics.
- script.save: Writes a whole file and answers with the file's diagnostics, the same way `edit` does.
- script.close: Closes the documents.
- script.format: Formats source through the pinned gdformat sidecar.
- script.hover: Hover documentation.
- script.completion: Completion items.
- script.signature_help: Signature help.
- script.definition: Go to definition.
- script.declaration: Go to declaration.
- script.references: Find references.
- script.highlights: Document highlights.
- script.diagnostics: Diagnostics the server published.
- script.document_symbols: Symbols of one document.
- script.workspace_symbols: Symbols across the worktree.
- script.prepare_rename: Checks whether a symbol can be renamed.
- script.rename: Plans a rename without writing, and refuses when the server plans nothing — every real rename touches at least the declaration, so an empty plan is the server declining rather than a rename that reached no files.
- script.apply_rename: Applies a planned rename in one transaction.

# debug
Operations:
- debug.status: Connects to the adapter and reports its capabilities. (not twice in one call: It takes no parameters, so a second one in the same call is the first one again.)
- debug.set_breakpoints: Replaces the breakpoints of one script.
- debug.breakpoint_locations: Validates candidate lines.
- debug.launch: Runs the project under the debugger. (only entry of its call: One debuggee, driven in order: each answer decides what the next call means.)
- debug.attach: Attaches to a game already running under this adapter. (not twice in one call: It takes no parameters, so a second one in the same call is the first one again.)
- debug.await_stop: Waits for the next stop. (only entry of its call: One debuggee, driven in order: each answer decides what the next call means.)
- debug.threads: Lists the debuggable threads. (not twice in one call: It takes no parameters, so a second one in the same call is the first one again.)
- debug.stack_trace: Returns the stopped stack, which is empty unless the game is stopped at a breakpoint or a step — a pause leaves it with no frame at all.
- debug.scopes: Returns Locals, Members, and Globals of a frame.
- debug.variables: Expands a scope or object.
- debug.evaluate: Evaluates an expression in a frame.
- debug.continue: Resumes the debuggee. (only entry of its call: One debuggee, driven in order: each answer decides what the next call means.)
- debug.pause: Pauses the debuggee between frames. (only entry of its call: One debuggee, driven in order: each answer decides what the next call means.)
- debug.step_over: Steps over one line. (only entry of its call: One debuggee, driven in order: each answer decides what the next call means.)
- debug.step_in: Steps into the call at the current line. (only entry of its call: One debuggee, driven in order: each answer decides what the next call means.)
- debug.step_out: Steps out of the current frame (emulated). (only entry of its call: One debuggee, driven in order: each answer decides what the next call means.)
- debug.restart: Restarts the debuggee with the last launch arguments. (only entry of its call: One debuggee, driven in order: each answer decides what the next call means.)
- debug.terminate: Stops the debuggee, keeping the adapter. (only entry of its call: One debuggee, driven in order: each answer decides what the next call means.)
- debug.disconnect: Detaches. (only entry of its call: One debuggee, driven in order: each answer decides what the next call means.)

# runtime
Operations:
- runtime.run: Runs the project and captures the first frame, unless `playArgs` start it with `--headless`, which draws none. (not twice in one call: There is one running game, so a second one in the same call is the first one again.)
- runtime.stop: Stops the running game. (not twice in one call: There is one running game, so a second one in the same call is the first one again.)
- runtime.restart: Restarts the running game. (not twice in one call: There is one running game, so a second one in the same call is the first one again.)
- runtime.get_state: Reports whether a game is running, its helper is ready, and the debugger has it paused at an error. (not twice in one call: It takes no parameters, so a second one in the same call is the first one again.)
- runtime.get_tree: Returns the running game's scene tree, and `paused`: whether the tree is paused right now.
- runtime.inspect_node: Inspects a running node.
- runtime.input: Injects input and captures the result. Each event names its kind and the parameters that kind uses, as {"kind": "key", "key": "A", "pressed": true} — send the release as a second event, or the key stays down. An event that leaves `pressed` out alternates on its own: the first is the press and the second the release, so a click is the same event written twice. A Button answers the release, not the press. A mouse_button event names its `button`, a joypad_button event its `joypadButton`, and a joypad_motion event its `axis`. A position is [x, y]. This drives the Input Map, so it is how you check that a level you built can actually be played. Its answer carries a frame, unless a later entry of the same call carries one too: a picture another picture replaces is not worth sending, and a moment in the middle of a key sequence is what capture is for.
- runtime.capture: Captures a PNG frame.
- runtime.wait: Lets the game run on for a few frames, then answers with how many passed and how long it took.
- runtime.pause: Freezes the running game where it stands, the way its own pause menu would: `SceneTree.paused`, so a node that opted out of pausing keeps running. (not twice in one call: It takes no parameters, so a second one in the same call is the first one again.)
- runtime.resume: Lets a paused game run on again. (not twice in one call: It takes no parameters, so a second one in the same call is the first one again.)
- runtime.get_monitors: Reads engine performance monitors.

# logs
Operations:
- logs.read: Reads a page.

# docs_search
Operations:
- docs_search.search: Retrieves ranked passages for a question in plain words.
- docs_search.ask: Answers one question from those same passages and hands back a paragraph and a quote instead of the chapters.

ops.description: The operations to run, in order, each with its parameters beside its `op`. One operation is a list of one; several run in this one call rather than one call each. These have to be the only entry of their call: debug.launch, debug.await_stop, debug.continue, debug.pause, debug.step_over, debug.step_in, debug.step_out, debug.restart, debug.terminate, debug.disconnect. These may sit beside others and may not appear twice: session.status, session.start, session.stop, session.get_state, session.answer_dialog, session.undo, session.redo, scene.list, scene.open, scene.save, scene.save_as, scene.reload, project.get_settings, project.list_autoloads, project.list_plugins, debug.status, debug.attach, debug.threads, runtime.run, runtime.stop, runtime.restart, runtime.get_state, runtime.pause, runtime.resume.
